Review round 1 (chain approx: self-authored, reviewer is the PR author; head 128b510d9bbaa99bed5729914faed6d36cd9f66f). Blocking: 1 finding. Not merged.

CI read per run from statusCheckRollup at this head: "Guards" PASS, "Lint, test, typecheck, build" PASS. No sensitive path touched (2 files: scripts/lib/is-main.mjs, scripts/lib/is-main.test.mjs). Scope matches the PR body.

**Finding 1 (MEDIUM, family 3: assertion that cannot fail, over a fail-open guard) — the "compares the wrong two things" half of the fix is untested.**
After this diff no test can fail if the comparison stops comparing. I applied this mutation to scripts/lib/is-main.mjs at 128b510:

```
return realpathSync(fileURLToPath(moduleUrl)) === realpathSync(process.argv[1]);
->
realpathSync(fileURLToPath(moduleUrl)); realpathSync(process.argv[1]); return true;
```

Result: `Tests 5 passed (5)`, no failures. So isMainModule returning true for every module whose path resolves would ship green, and every one of the 16 callers would then run its main when imported by a test. Cause: the existing "is false for an unrelated module URL" test uses `file:///not/the/entry/point.mjs`, which did exercise the inequality on main, but with realpathSync it now throws ENOENT and is answered by the catch branch, never by `===`. The new missing-file test pins that same branch. Nothing passes two paths that both exist and differ. (By contrast removing the try/catch fails 2 of 5 tests, so the catch is pinned; the comparison is not.)
Fix: add a case where moduleUrl is a real, existing file that is not argv[1], e.g. `expect(isMainModule(pathToFileURL(path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "is-main.mjs")).href)).toBe(false)` (argv[1] is the vitest runner/worker, so the two exist and differ), or an in-fixture negative: a second fixture file imported (not run) by the entry that prints nothing for its own isMainModule. Re-run the mutation above and report it failing.

**Verified, no finding:**
- Symlink test vs origin/main's is-main.mjs (applied myself): fails 3/3 with `expected '' not to be ''`; with the fix passes 3/3 (5 tests).
- Missing-file test passes on old code (no throw there either), as the PR body admits; it is not an empty assertion on the new code (removing try/catch fails it), so acceptable as a pin on the catch. The header claim "is-main.test.mjs covers the missing-file case" is accurate.
- Windows claim: the header claims only that separators agree (both sides native paths via fileURLToPath/realpathSync), which is what the code does. It does not claim drive-letter case or 8.3-name normalisation (JS realpathSync does not canonicalise those; unchanged from before). Header matches code.
- Callers: `grep -rln isMainModule scripts` prints 20 files = is-main.mjs + its test + 2 other tests + 16 entry scripts. 16 is correct; the bead's "17" matches the count of files that mention `lib/is-main` (incl. lib/git-diff.mjs and release-cost-report.test.mjs, comment-only mentions).
- Through /tmp (symlink to /private/tmp) with --help: check-unreachable-beads 671 bytes on branch, 0 bytes on main's is-main; check-pr-title 468 bytes on branch, 0 on main.

Families: 1 (comment claims guarantee) checked, nothing found; 2 (wrong two things) checked, nothing in the code, the test gap is reported as family 3; 3 (assertion that cannot fail) 1 finding above; 4 (sibling-omission) checked, gh-app-token.mjs and check-bead-dispatch.mjs workarounds are out of scope and listed as follow-ups, no other isMainModule-style raw argv/URL comparison among the callers. Absence: no existing-vs-existing-differing-path test, read at scripts/lib/is-main.test.mjs @ 128b510.
Whole-file read (4.3): scripts/lib/is-main.mjs read whole, clean; scripts/lib/is-main.test.mjs read whole, Finding 1.
